title: Preserve backend RNG state for discarded prefill samples
applies_when: A seeded inference sampler consumes random draws for unfinished prompt chunks or other outputs that the scheduler subsequently discards, especially when a CPU backend inherits GPU bookkeeping.
lesson: A discarded output must not silently advance the accepted request's seeded sequence. Trace both the sampling draw and its rollback through the actual backend. CPU torch.Generator does not support the device-offset rewind used by this GPU model-runner path. Snapshot the affected CPU generators before sampling and restore their opaque state afterward; simply skipping the unsupported offset call can keep generation alive but change token IDs with the chunk size. Compare multiple seeded prompts, including one that fits in a single chunk, across unchunked and at least two chunk budgets, then make an ordinary follow-up request. Check actual module/backend identity and preserve both the crashing baseline and a healthy-but-wrong skip-only control. Do not equate absence of an exception with reproducibility.
avoid_when: This witness uses a tiny random Llama, direct token input, Linux CPU/Torch2.14 and exact parent/author runner-module overlays on an official e68 CPU distribution. It is not a full PR build, trained-model accuracy/convergence, HTTP health, speculative decoding, CUDA/MPS, model-parallel or all-platform validation. Do not replace a supported device offset path with full-state copies universally: synchronization, state format and sampling contracts differ. MRV2 uses different randomness and is not qualified by an MRV1 witness. An owner-selected public known bug is not a prospective discovery or evidence-selection efficacy result.

evidence.note: Public CPU failure report: a seeded request split by chunked prefill reaches CPU Generator.get_offset and kills the worker. Unseeded or unchunked controls work. Reported original platform is macOS/Torch2.13, not the independently checked Linux environment.

Author repair snapshots only discarded requests' CPU generator states before the real sampler/rejection sampler, restores afterward, and retains offset rewind for other devices. Source mechanism; it does not establish GPU performance or all sampler-mode correctness.

Scoped native fixture and conditions: parent chunk16 fails; author module unchunked/chunk16/chunk32 produces matching three-seed token IDs and healthy follow-ups. A controlled skip-only parent variant generates successfully but changes seeded tokens. Branch link is mutable: resolve its commit and recheck source/environment before reuse. No competing PR, model accuracy, speedup, complete upstream build/CI or prospective-selector claim.
